article.headline: SailPoint Bounces 3.9% After Hours Following 6.7% Drop In Tech Selloff
article.deck: The October breakout past the 22.38 buy point has stalled; the stock closed 17.8% below it and under its 50-day line, so there is no entry until it rebuilds.
body: SailPoint rose 0.71, or 3.9%, to 19.10 after hours as of 5:00 p.m. Eastern. That followed a 1.33 drop, or 6.7%, to 18.39 in the regular session, when the stock traded 1.1x its 50-day average volume. The close sits 17.8% below the 22.38 buy point of a five-week cup that ran 17.8% deep, with a buy range up to 23.50. The stock broke out on Oct. 27, trading 0.65x its average that day, and seven sessions later it is a stalled breakout well below the buy point.

The cup formed after a bigger correction, from a 24.00 high on Oct. 6, 2025, to a 10.30 low on April 10, and the stock is still below that earlier high. Thursday's drop took it 7.9% under its 50-day line at 19.97 and below the 21-day line at 20.14, with the high also under that line, a reading of -0.52 ATRs from the 21-day line. It stays 14.3% above its 200-day line at 16.09. The stock is 18.7% off its 52-week high of 22.62 and down 9.1% this year. It ranks 62 of 99 on the desk's list, and its RS line is 20.6% off its high.

SailPoint still loses money. It lost 9 cents a share in the quarter ended July 31 on revenue of $308.8 million, up 16.8% from a year earlier. It lost 13 cents, 6 cents and 6 cents in the three quarters before that. Next earnings are due Dec. 15.
The last run came on Oct. 23, when a headline said SailPoint soared 11% as cybersecurity stocks rallied, and Zacks upgraded the shares to buy that day.
article.watch: Whether the after-hours bounce carries the stock back above the 50-day line at 19.97.

article.headline: Grainger Holds Near Highs After Best Revenue Growth In Five Years
article.deck: A day after clearing a 15-week flat base at 1420.01, the stock closed 2.2% above the buy point and inside a buy range that runs to 1491.01.
body: W.W. Grainger sells the things that keep buildings and factories running: safety and security gear, material handling and storage equipment, pumps and plumbing parts, cleaning supplies, metalworking and hand tools. It also manages inventory and gives technical support. Its customers run from small shops to large corporations and government agencies, mostly in North America, Japan and the United Kingdom. It sells through two arms: a hands-on business for North American accounts and an online business built around a huge catalog.

The latest quarter in the payload, the one ended June 30, showed earnings of $12.01 a share, up 20.5% from a year earlier, on revenue of $5.02 billion, up 10.3%. Earnings have climbed in each of the last four quarters, from $6.12 to $9.44 to $11.65 to $12.01. Revenue rose from $4.43 billion to $4.74 billion to $5.02 billion over the last three of them.

The company reported its third quarter Wednesday. Headlines from its earnings call pointed to double-digit sales growth, and Investor's Business Daily ran a headline saying Grainger surged on its best revenue growth in five years. The payload carries no figures from that report beyond what the headlines say.
The market values Grainger at about $68.4 billion, or 28.4 times forward earnings. The stock is up 43.8% this year and 51.8% over the past year.

The report sent the stock past the 1420.01 buy point of a 15-week flat base on Wednesday, trading 2.39x its 50-day average volume that day. The base ran 12.9% deep, from a July 17 high to a Sept. 28 low. On Thursday the stock gave back 38.00, or 2.6%, to 1451.39 as the Nasdaq fell 5.5%, trading 2.0x its average. The close is still 2.2% above the buy point and inside the buy range, which runs to 1491.01. It was unchanged after hours.

Grainger sits 4.6% below its 52-week high of 1521.41 and 10.8% above its 50-day line at 1309.74. It is 2.12 ATRs above the 21-day line at 1362.12, firm but short of a stretched reading. It ranks 92 of 99 on the desk's list, and its RS line hit a new high on a day the indexes broke down. Industrial is one of the weaker groups on the desk, with 12% of its names above the 50-day line, so Grainger is leading it on its own.
The breakout came into a market the desk rates in correction, with the Nasdaq carrying 7.5 weighted distribution days. Next earnings are due Feb. 2.
article.watch: Whether the stock holds the 1420.01 buy point while the indexes stay in correction.

chief.verdict: The Nasdaq fell 5.5% to 24315.0 and now sits 8.2% below its 50-day line, 3.1% below its 200-day and 12.3% off its high. Only three names are in a buy range (GWW, AMGN, PFE). The leadership left standing is defensive: healthcare has an average RS of 67 with 71% of its names above the 50-day, while ai infra (RS 21) and energy both have 0% above the 50-day and ai chips has 4%. Most bases on the screen are deep cups sitting 25% to 90% below their pivots. The risk leans down, and the stocks that broke out are the ones to protect, not to add to.

It closed at 1451.39, 2.2% past the pivot, but it is 2.12 ATRs above its 21-day line and 10.8% above its 50-day, and it fell 2.6% on volume 2.0 times normal the day after the breakout. In a correction that is not a place to start a position.
